## Overview

This vignette demonstrates a **single-run** workflow for predicting oxygen isotope ratios (δ18O) using oxyproxy, both step by step through the individual pipeline functions and in a single call with `OxyProxy()`.

All examples use the **Herbivore Standard**, a self-consistent reference animal built into oxyproxy:

| Parameter | Herbivore Standard value |
|-----------|--------------------------|
| Body mass | 30 kg |
| Water economy index (WEI) | 0.25 |
| Digestibility of food | 0.7 |
| Carbohydrate content | 0.85 |
| Protein content | 0.1 |
| Fat content | 0.05 |
| Free water content of food | 0.65 |
| Air temperature | 15 °C |
| Surface water δ18O | −3.25 ‰ |
| Relative humidity | 0.75 |

## Load the package

```{r}
library(oxyproxy)

# If you're developing locally and not installed:
# devtools::load_all()
```

## Step 1 — Species physiology (single value)

`Species()` expects `body_mass` and `water_economy_index` (plus optional `changeConstant`).

```{r}
species_out <- Species(
  body_mass = 30, # kg
  water_economy_index = 0.25, # typical range ~0.05-0.6
  changeConstant = FALSE
)

str(species_out)
```

## Step 2 — Diet composition (single value)

`Food()` expects:
`digestibility_of_food`, `Carbohydrate_Content`, `Protein_Content`, `Fat_Content`, and `Free_Water_Content_Food`.

```{r}
food_out <- Food(
  digestibility_of_food = 0.7,
  Carbohydrate_Content = 0.85,
  Protein_Content = 0.1,
  Fat_Content = 0.05, # NOTE: carbohydrate + protein + fat must sum to 1
  Free_Water_Content_Food = 0.65,
  changeConstant = FALSE
)

str(food_out)
```

## Step 3 — Environment (single value)

`Environment()` expects `air_temperature`, `relative_humidity`, and `d18O_surface_water`.

```{r}
env_out <- Environment(
  air_temperature = 15, # Celsius
  relative_humidity = 0.75, # proportion between 0 and 1 (not a percentage)
  d18O_surface_water = -3.25 # per mil (‰ VSMOW)
)

env_out
```

## Step 4 — Inputs -> Outputs -> d18O body water

### 4A) Oxygen inputs

`Inputs()` combines species, food, and environment into oxygen input variables:

```{r}
inputs_out <- Inputs(
  species = species_out,
  food = food_out,
  environment = env_out
)

str(inputs_out)
```

### 4B) Oxygen outputs

`Outputs()` computes the oxygen output variables:

```{r}
outputs_out <- Outputs(
  inputs = inputs_out,
  sweating_species = FALSE
)

str(outputs_out)
```

### 4C) Final isotope estimates

`d18Obw_Estimation()` computes the final body water, phosphate, and carbonate isotope estimates:

```{r}
d18o_out <- d18Obw_Estimation(outputs = outputs_out)

head(d18o_out[, c("d18Obw", "d18Ophos", "d18Ocarb")])
```

## Alternative — Call `OxyProxy()`

`OxyProxy()` runs the full pipeline in one call. It does **not** accept `species=`, `food=`, `environment=`;
instead it accepts a set of `model_*` inputs, which can be single values (as here) or vectors (see the
Vectorized Inputs vignette). With the same Herbivore Standard values, the result matches Step 4C:

```{r}
oxyproxy_out <- OxyProxy(
  model_bodymass = 30,
  model_WaterEconomyIndex = 0.25,
  model_Digestibility_of_food = 0.7,
  model_Carbohydrate_Content = 0.85,
  model_Protein_Content = 0.1,
  model_Fat_Content = 0.05,
  model_Free_Water_Content_Food = 0.65,
  model_air_temperature = 15,
  model_Relative_Humidity = 0.75,
  model_d18O_surfacewater = -3.25,
  changeConstant = FALSE,
  sweating_species = FALSE,
  PlotRange = FALSE # avoid plots in vignette by default
)

head(oxyproxy_out[, c("d18Obw", "d18Ophos", "d18Ocarb")])
```

## Inspecting results

```{r}
names(d18o_out)
str(d18o_out, max.level = 1)
```
